subject: Communication
title: Emotional Agility in Difficult Conversations
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Emotional Agility in Difficult Conversations.

hook.text: Susan David was 15 when her father died. A teacher handed her a notebook: 'Write what you feel.'

buildup.text: David's concept of 'emotional agility' means holding emotions loosely — neither suppressing them nor being controlled.

discovery.text: The shift is linguistic: from 'I am angry' (identity) to 'I notice I'm feeling anger' (observation).

twist.text: Forced positivity — 'just think happy thoughts' — is as rigid as being stuck in negativity.

climax.text: Emotional agility in conversations means being present, choosing responses that align with values, and adapting as things change.

punchline.text: Emotions are visitors. You are the home. Welcome them, but don't let them redecorate.

quiz.question: What does emotional agility mean, according to Susan David?
options: Holding emotions loosely without being controlled by them
